Guidelines11 recommend that patients who develop erythrocy- tosis secondary to hypoxic pulmonary disease should first be considered for methods to improve oxygenation, including long- term oxygen therapy. Those who have hyperviscosity or a hae- matocrit greater than 56% should undergo venesection. ACE in- hibitors or angiotensin II receptor antagonists might be of use for patients who do not tolerate venesection;11 beneficial responses have been reported with enalapril in altitude polycythaemia,12 and with losartan in erythrocytosis secondary to chronic obstruc- tive pulmonary disease.13 Theophylline has also been reported to be of benefit. 1.
